Quick response with a simple “rotation playbook” we use when customers span US/EU/APAC. Two options depending on how much scheduling overhead you want:

Option 1 — Weekly rotating slots (recommended)
- Pick three slots spaced ~89hours apart. Each week the mid-day slot cycles to the next region so no one team gets stuck always on late.
- Example (local conversions):
  * Slot A: Wed 16:00 UTC — Boston (12:00 EDT), Amsterdam (18:00 CEST), Singapore (00:00 SGT next day)
  * Slot B: Wed 00:00 UTC — Boston (20:00 EDT), Amsterdam (02:00 CEST next day), Singapore (10:00 SGT)
  * Slot C: Wed 08:00 UTC — Boston (04:00 EDT), Amsterdam (10:00 CEST), Singapore (16:00 SGT)
- Rotation idea: Week 1 = Slot C (APAC-friendly), Week 2 = Slot A (EU-friendly), Week 3 = Slot B (US-friendly). Repeat.

Option 2 — Biweekly compromise (single slot)
- One weekly time that is early morning for Boston, late afternoon for Amsterdam, evening for Singapore. Simpler to manage but less equitable.

Session format we recommend: 15min setup (keys/test data), 4590min live integration + verification, 159min procurement/next-steps wrap.

Prep checklist for the technical run (Dylan can confirm specifics):
- A service account or API key with a short-lived test token (please provide via secure channel)
- Minimal sample dataset (S3 link or sanitized CSV)
- Allowed IP ranges for our SE machines (if you have network restrictions)

Marissa 99cc9for procurement coordination. If you want, we can send recurring calendar invites with a rotation rule and guard rails (no recordings unless agreed).

I attached a short playbook PDF (Redwood-demo-playbook.pdf) with the rotation examples and what we do during each minute block.

If Jun 28 works we can start rotation the week of Jun 28 and run 3 weeks to validate cadence. Let me know final attendee list and any recording/NDAs constraints.

Best,
Soojin
